previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with advanced multiple sclerosis, neurogenic bladder with a suprapubic catheter, and a history of recurrent UTIs, was admitted after a witnessed seizure with tongue biting and aspiration. He was found to have hyponatremia likely due to excessive water intake, and imaging revealed encephalomalacia as a possible seizure focus. He developed aspiration pneumonia requiring antibiotics and was intubated briefly for airway protection. His sodium corrected, seizures were controlled with levetiracetam, and he improved clinically. A video swallow study showed mild aspiration initially but cleared him for ground foods and thin liquids with a recommendation to start meals with pureed foods. He was discharged home with services, on Keppra for seizure prevention, with follow-up planned for neurology, dermatology, and primary care, and instructions for wound care and baclofen pump refill.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with PNA, ICU stay, PICC RN tried at the bedside
x3 and failed on apixaban.  Please place PICC

COMPARISON:  None.

TECHNIQUE:
OPERATORS: Dr. ___ Interventional ___ and Dr. ___
___, Interventional Radiology fellow performed the procedure.
ANESTHESIA: Local 1% lidocaine.
MEDICATIONS:
CONTRAST: None.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  32 seconds, 1.5 mGy

PROCEDURE:
1. Double lumen PICC placement through the left basilic vein.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the left
basilic vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a
micropuncture set. Permanent ultrasound images were obtained before and after
intravenous access, which confirmed vein patency. A peel-away sheath was then
placed over a guidewire. The guidewire was then advanced into the superior
vena cava using fluoroscopic guidance. A double lumen PIC line measuring 49 cm
in length was then placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned
in the distal SVC under fluoroscopic guidance. Position of the catheter was
confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot film of the chest. The peel-away sheath and
guidewire were then removed. The catheter was secured to the skin, flushed,
and a sterile dressing applied.
The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no immediate
complications.

FINDINGS: 

1.  The accessed vein was patent and compressible.
2.  Basilicvein approach double lumen left PICC with tip in the distal SVC.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful placement of a left 49 cm basilic approach double lumen PowerPICC
with tip in the distal SVC.  The line is ready to use.
